event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: The filing contains only one explicit reference to pandemic-style disruptions: management warns that supply-chain breakdowns and labour shortages could delay projects and raise costs by limiting the availability of materials, equipment and contractors.  Although the company never names COVID-19, these very disruptions are emblematic of the post-2020 pandemic environment, so the sentence functions as a forward-looking disclosure that such conditions could persist or recur.  Because the language is conditional ("may experience") and un-quantified, the identified risk is potential rather than a currently booked impact, which tempers severity.  Nevertheless, the acknowledgement of concrete operational consequences—delays and cost inflation— elevates the importance above a boiler-plate mention.  Given that the pandemic began less than four years before the February 2024 filing and continues to influence global logistics and labour markets, the Time Decay Principle allows a mid-to-high score; overall, the evidence supports a moderate-high risk rating.

evidence_list.snippet: We may also experience unforeseen delays and increased project costs as a result of supply chain disruptions and labor shortages, which may impact the availability of equipment and materials needed for, and availability of contractors to work on, our construction projects.

components.reason: Explicitly cites "supply chain disruptions," a hallmark pandemic impact that can cripple operations.
Identifies "labor shortages," another widespread COVID-19 related pressure on companies.
Specifies concrete operational consequences—"unforeseen delays" and "increased project costs"—demonstrating material exposure.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: The sentence links supply-chain and labour constraints to cost overruns and schedule slippage, mapping directly to pandemic-era risks; the combined aggravating factors justify a score of 7 within the recent-event range.
